sections.html:
Two county offices share the work. The Assessment Office sets and maintains the value of every parcel. The Revenue and Tax Claim Office sends the bills, takes the payments and follows up on anything unpaid. Both are in the government center at 669 Washington Street in Easton, and a separate body, the Revenue Appeals Board, hears assessment disputes.

Assessment is in Room 2112 on the second floor, phone 610-829-6155. Revenue and Tax Claim answers at 610-829-6186. When you sell, you will usually need two things from these offices: the parcel's current assessment and a tax certification that shows what is owed. Appeal fees are set by county council resolution.

File with the Revenue Appeals Board by August 1. An annual appeal filed by that date gets a hearing, and any change applies to the following tax year.

Assessment appeal rules, procedures revised June 15, 2026
StepRule
Annual appeal deadlineAugust 1
Interim appeal after a notice of change40 days from the notice date
Residential filing fee$25 per parcel
Commercial or exemption filing fee$250 per parcel
Hearing noticeAt least 20 days before the hearing
Supporting documents due10 business days before the hearing
Appeal of a board decision to court30 days from the mailing date

Each parcel needs its own application, signed by the record owner whose name is on the deed. The filing fee is not refunded.

  • Residential forms must list the most recent comparable sales. Without them the assessment may stay as it is.
  • A residential property assessed at $175,000 or more needs an appraisal by a state certified appraiser.
  • Restricted appraisal reports are not accepted.
  • Filing can raise the assessment as well as lower it, and the board warns about that risk.

sections.h2: If you miss the August deadline
sections.html:
Owners who miss August 1 wait for the next one, unless the county mails a notice of change. That notice opens a 40-day interim window. Hearings for the 2026 season ran from August 5 through October 29.

The board will move a hearing once, for a $25 fee. An appellant who does not show up is treated as having abandoned the appeal and loses the right to go on to the Court of Common Pleas. The county posts the Common Level Ratio each July 1. Before deciding that an appeal is worth the effort, ask the Assessment Office for the current figure and for recent comparable sales near the parcel.

The exclusion trims the assessed value used to compute school property tax on a primary residence. Under Act 72 of 2004, school districts draw on state gaming revenue and local income taxes to give every approved homestead the same dollar reduction before the tax is figured.

  • Applications go to the county Assessment Office and are due by March 1.
  • It covers one primary residence, so a second home does not qualify.
  • Report a change in use within 45 days, such as turning the house into a rental.
  • A denied application can be appealed within 40 days of the date on the letter.
  • A false application brings back taxes, interest, a 10 percent penalty and possible misdemeanor charges.

Some school boards choose not to adopt the exclusion, so ask your school district what applies. If you are moving out, tell the assessor. A house that stops being a homestead should not keep the exclusion.

The county runs an online portal for current taxes, and the 2026 real estate tax portal is live. Card payments carry a 3.5 percent fee, and electronic checks under $29,999 cost $4.

Past-due accounts are handled by phone at 610-829-6186. The county anticipates a separate way to pay balances less than two years behind that are not subject to sale, so ask the Revenue Office which option fits your parcel.

The same page links the tax certification that a closing agent requests. Order it early rather than in the last week before closing, because a certification that shows an old balance can hold up the file.

Unpaid taxes go to the Tax Claim Bureau and can end in a tax sale. The county holds a Judicial Sale in late May and an Upset Sale in September, both at 1:00 p.m. in Courtroom 1. The 2026 sales were May 27 and September 24.

State law adopted in House Bill 264 of 2021 requires bidders to register before any tax sale. For the 2026 upset sale, registration ran from August 31 through September 14 and was available only at the courthouse government center in Easton, with no exceptions.

If you have a lapsed bill, contact the Revenue Office well before September and ask the Tax Claim Office what clearing the account would take. A seller who is behind should tell the title agent at the start, so the payoff can be built into the closing statement.

sections.h2: Look up your assessment before listing
sections.html:
The Assessment Office links a public site, ncpub.org, where county assessment data can be reviewed online. Search by address or parcel, then compare the assessed value with recent sales of similar houses on your street.

  • Write down the tax map identification: district, map, block and lot. Appeals and the homestead form both ask for it.
  • Check the school district and municipality listed for the parcel, because the homestead application asks for both.
  • Look at the building details, such as rooms, baths, garage and lot size, and report any error to the office.
  • Confirm whether a homestead exclusion is already applied before you sell.

Buyers ask what the tax bill looks like, and a printed parcel record answers most of it. The Assessment Office also has a change of address form for a bill that still goes to an old mailing address.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or an open appeal
sections.html:
A sale does not wait for the tax calendar. If a balance is due, the title company will list it as a payoff at closing and take it out of your proceeds. Call 610-829-6186 for a current figure, and ask for the tax certification at the same time.

If you filed an appeal and the hearing is still ahead, tell your agent or buyer. A change from the board applies to the next tax year, so the result will not alter the bill the buyer sees at closing. A cash buyer can close without waiting on lender appraisal rules, which helps when a county balance needs to be cleared quickly.

The federal estimate for 2025 is 324,411 residents, up 3.7 percent from the 2020 base. The latest five-year survey puts the median owned home at $308,600, median household income at $89,184 and median gross rent at $1,395. Easton is the county seat and Bethlehem is the largest city. Every city, borough and township sits inside the same assessment system, so your parcel record is a better guide to your own tax bill than any county average.

faqs.q: What is the last day to challenge an assessment in Northampton County?
faqs.a: August 1. A yearly appeal reaches the Revenue Appeals Board only if it is filed by then, and any result applies to the next tax year. Interim appeals get 40 days from a notice of change.

faqs.q: What does it cost to file an assessment appeal?
faqs.a: $25 per parcel for a residential appeal and $250 for a commercial or exemption appeal. The money is not refunded, and moving a hearing costs another $25.

faqs.q: Does an appeal require an appraisal?
faqs.a: Yes, once the residential assessed value reaches $175,000. A state certified appraiser must prepare it, and restricted reports are refused.

faqs.q: By when must an owner request the homestead exclusion?
faqs.a: By March 1, filed with the county Assessment Office. The office sends a written notice if the request is denied.

faqs.q: How long do I have to take a board decision to court?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the mailing date of the board's notice, filed in the Court of Common Pleas. An appellant who abandoned the hearing gives up that right.
